<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par121 />{{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=9|verse=2}}, 3;<ref>Analogous to {{GHGheb|text=הַלָּבוּשׁ הַבַּדִּים|translate=who was clothed in linen}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=9|verse=3}}, would be {{GHGheb|text=וְהַנּוֹתָר אֶת־הֶהָמוֹן הַזֶּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=31|verse=10}}; but we must certainly read there {{GHGheb|text=וַנּוֹתֵר}} with the LXX.—Still less can {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=87|verse=3}} be so explained, {{GHGheb|text=נִכְבָּדוֹת}} being not an accusative, but the subject of a noun-clause. On the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלוּחַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=14|verse=6}} may be explained with Ewald in the sense of ''being charged with'' something, so that, like {{GHGheb|text=צִוָּח}}, it may be construed with an accusative.</ref> with the accusative preceding, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=4|verse=12}}.—(''b'') with {{GHGterm|verba copiae}} and ''inopiae'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=1|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=38|verse=10}} (equivalent to ''I must forego the residue of my years''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=40|verse=20}}.—(''c'') an accusative of the result ({{GHGpar|117|ii}}) with the passive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=14|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=28|verse=2}}; with the accusative preceding, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=24|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=3|verse=12}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=26|verse=18}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=15|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=22|verse=16|hidebook=1}}.<ref>In reality {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּרֻם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=20}}, 26 (''it became putrid'') is equivalent to a passive (''it was changed''), to which {{GHGheb|text=תּֽוֹלָעִים}} is added as an accusative of the result.</ref> Also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=40|verse=17}} and 46:23, the accusative preceding {{GHGheb|text=עָשׂוּי}} (in 41:18 following it) can only be taken as the accusative of the result; some general idea, such as that of ''place'', is to be understood as the subject of {{GHGheb|text=עָשׂוּי}}.—(''d'') an accusative of the member or part specially affected by the action ({{GHGpar|117|ll}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=17|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=14|verse=24|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=1|verse=7}} (accusative ''before'' part. pass.); {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=15|verse=32}} (accusative with suffix after the part. pass.).

{{GHGmargin-letter|121|e}}
2. Both accusatives are retained in an unusual manner after the passive of a {{GHGterm|verbum implendi}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=21}}; instead, however, of the ''Niph.'' {{GHGheb|text=וְיִמָּלֵא}} the {{GHGterm|Qal}} (which is sometimes used transitively elsewhere) should simply be read with the LXX; similarly in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=72|verse=19}}, although there the LXX also translate the passive.

{{GHGmargin-letter|121|f}}
'''3.''' The efficient cause (or personal agent) is, as a rule, attached to the passive by {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} (thus corresponding to the Greek and Latin dative), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=25|verse=21}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּעָ֫תֶ֫ר לוֹ יְהֹוָה|translate=the Lord let himself be intreated by him}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=26|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=10}} and the blessing {{GHGheb|text=בָּרוּךְ הוּא לַֽיהוָֹה|translate=blessed be he of the Lord}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=2|verse=20}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=14|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=17|verse=2}}b, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=15|verse=13}}; also in the plural, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=23|verse=21}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=2|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=115|verse=15}}).—''Before'' the verb, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=14|verse=20}} and frequently; less commonly by {{GHGheb|text=מִן־}} (called {{GHGheb|text=מִן־}} of origin=''coming from''), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=11}}; ''before'' the verb, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=37|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=1}}; by {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} (''instrumenti'') [rarely, König § 106], {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=6}} ({{GHGheb|text=בָּֽאָדָם|translate=by man}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=36|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=3}} b [but ?=''wherewith it was worked'' ({{GHGpar|52|e}}) ''with thee''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=21|verse=3}}, König § 106; and see {{GHGheb|text=עָבַד בְּ}} in the Lexicon], {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=14|verse=4}}, always to introduce a personal agent.—On the connexion of the passive participle with a genitive of the agent, cf. {{GHGpar|116|l}}.<section end=par121 />

Stade, Giessen, 1881 ff., and since 1907 by K. Marti.}}}} 1905, p. 325 ff. (supplementing Albrecht’s work by a treatment of the gender of many nouns in the Mishna); and his ‘Notizen aus der tannaitischen Literatur...’ {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZAW.|Zeitschrift für die alttestamentliche Wissenschaft, ed. by B. Stade, Giessen, 1881 ff., and since 1907 by K. Marti.}}}} 1908, p. 144 ff.</div>
